title: Taking away
examples: Teacher, if I have five apples and I eat two, how many are left?
What do I do when I take some things away from a group?
Can you show me taking away with my fingers?

explain.say: Look at this picture. We see five bright red balloons.
Now, two balloons float away into the blue sky.
We started with five, and we took away two. How many are left?
If you have seven cookies and you give three to your friend, how many do you keep?
When we take away, we are finding the number that is remaining.

items: Start with a group of things

explain.say: Imagine you have ten crayons and you use four for a drawing.

faq.a: Taking away means subtraction. It tells us how many are left when some are removed from a group.
asks: How do I find how many are left?

faq.q: Is taking away always the same as counting backwards?
faq.a: Yes, for small numbers, counting backwards is a great way to help you take away. You just count down from the starting number.
asks: Can I count backwards to take away?

faq.q: Do I need to know my number facts to take away?
faq.a: Knowing your number facts helps you, but you can also use your fingers or draw pictures to help you count what is left.
asks: What if I forget my number facts?
Can I use my fingers for subtraction?

faq.q: Does the order matter when I take away?
faq.a: Yes, the order matters a lot. Taking away two from five is not the same as taking away five from two.
asks: Is 5 minus 2 the same as 2 minus 5?
Does the big number always go first?

faq.q: What if I take away more than I have?
faq.a: If you try to take away more than you have, you will have zero left. You cannot have negative balloons!
asks: Can I take away ten from three?
What is the answer if I take away too much?

facts: Subtraction is the process of taking one number away from another.
The symbol for taking away is the minus sign.
If you start with a group and remove some, you are finding the difference.

quiz.say: If you have eight stars and three fall off, how many stars remain?
quiz.why: You count back from eight three times: seven, six, five. So five stars are left.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you are adding the numbers together instead of taking them away.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only took away one number, not the correct amount.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only subtracted the smaller number from itself.

quiz.say: Ten fingers are shown. If you hide five, how many are visible?
quiz.why: You start at ten and count back five spots to find the remaining number.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you added the numbers instead of subtracting.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you did not take away any fingers at all.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you subtracted the smaller number from the larger number incorrectly.

quiz.say: What is the result of four minus zero?
quiz.why: If you take away nothing from a group, you still have the same amount.

wrong.1: This is wrong because taking away nothing keeps the original amount.
wrong.2: This is wrong because zero cannot be the number you start with if you are taking away nothing.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you subtracted one extra time when you should have taken away nothing.
